EMBEDDED TO CLOUD

Peak HydroMet

I built the station firmware, data pipeline, and dashboard widgets as the sole developer.

The nRF52840 reads Davis station data over RS-485 and converts it to JSON before sending it by LoRaWAN or cellular. Downstream tools can work with one format for dashboards and anomaly detection.

OPEN MAP DATA

Organic Maps

I authored the cycling classification and rendering proposal in PR #12692.

The proposal distinguishes shared lanes, painted lanes, and protected tracks while preserving each road’s classification. Side-aware data lets the renderer place those indicators where cyclists encounter them.

Compare the map screenshotsRead Organic Maps PR #12692
WEB PERFORMANCE

SharedLens

I built the gallery and its viewport-prioritized thumbnail loader.

The gallery was used at five weddings with more than 100 guests. I capped thumbnail loading at four concurrent requests and prioritized photos near the viewport. Multipart S3 uploads report progress for large media files.

Try the loading queueVisit SharedLens

ORGANIC MAPS · PR #12692

Cycling lines on a real map

The released cycling layer draws bike routes in purple. My PR makes three kinds of infrastructure visible at a glance, using dotted, dashed, and solid lines.

How to read the lines

1. Dotted · Shared travel lane

2. Dashed · Painted bike lane

3. Solid · Physically separated track

Read the implementation in PR #12692

Android Emulator captures at the same downtown Vancouver center and zoom. The release uses its downloadable regional map. The PR uses a Vancouver test map with the cycling data it needs. Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors.
